items.summary: 💯 In so many of my purchasing decisions these days I get frustrated that there is nothing that I want and I am getting scalped by crazy high prices for the most ordinary basic stuff The basic end conc…
items.body:
💯

In so many of my purchasing decisions these days I get frustrated that there is nothing that I want and I am getting scalped by crazy high prices for the most ordinary basic stuff

The basic end conclusion then is: I have to rip out the middle men

In case of furniture, the answer is design it myself and go to a carpenter to build it

There's going to be a big revival of artisanal jobs I think

quote.display_name: Stewart Alsop - Host of Crazy Wisdom Radio Show
quote.text:
this leads to higher quality over time

information arbitrage from people who dont want to put in the work of creativity (opposite of hustle cult) is going away

comments.display_name: Stewart Alsop - Host of Crazy Wisdom Radio Show
comments.text:
have you thought about cutting out another middle man and learning carpentry too?

I'm not there yet but I think ill end up there, just building whatever I want using the vast armory of tools we now have (and what do when creation gets too easy with anything regarding software,
comments.text_zh:
你有没有想过再去掉一个中间商，连木工也自己学？

我还没到那一步，但我觉得自己最终会到那一步，只是用我们现在拥有的那一大套工具（以及当软件相关的任何创造都变得太容易时该怎么办，

comments.text:
I have some experience here. A carpenter is going to cost 10-100X what you pay in store for ready-made furniture. Mass production is really efficient. You don’t go to a carpenter to save money. You go for customization.

A low-end store like ikea sometimes sells furniture cheaper
comments.text_zh:
这方面我有些经验。请木匠做，成本会是你在店里买现成家具的 10 到 100 倍。大规模生产真的很高效。找木匠不是为了省钱，是为了定制。

IKEA 这类低端商店有时卖的家具更便宜

comments.text: Or just make furniture your new hobby. Cheaper than therapy and you get a table out of it.
comments.text_zh: 或者把做家具当成新爱好。比心理咨询便宜，还能做出一张桌子。

comments.text: Artisan jobs are already lined up for a big comeback; with AI forcing people out of “easy” office jobs, they will have no choice but to learn something that buyers don't want AI for: artisanry.
comments.text_zh: 手工艺岗位已经在迎来一次大回归；随着 AI 把人从「轻松」的办公室工作中挤出去，他们将别无选择，只能去学买家不想用 AI 来做的事：手艺。

comments.text: maybe the future is less buying and more making things ourselves
comments.text_zh: 也许未来会更少购买，更多地自己动手做东西

items.summary: Scary NGINX vulnerability, but I checked and my VPS servers already had auto upgraded to the new one! Very very very very very important to enable auto upgrades now, I even have auto reboot, which is…
items.body:
Scary NGINX vulnerability, but I checked and my VPS servers already had auto upgraded to the new one!

Very very very very very important to enable auto upgrades now, I even have auto reboot, which is a bit risky if you're not present, but I care more about my sites being up to date and safe than offline for a few hours

And generally security updates/upgrades are tested and safe

quote.text: 🚨 Critical NGINX Vulnerabilities: @wiz_io Research, alongside @xint_official , @MetnirAI , @rapid7 , @ikotas00 independently discovered 2 critical memory-safety flaws in NGINX (CVE-2026-123633 & CVE-2026-123007) allowing unauthenticated RCE with HTTP/2 enabled.

comments.text: on the flip side, supply chain attacks are also rampant. i'd set at least a small delay on auto-updates. unless maybe the authors are posting about it. but that can also be compromised of course.
comments.text_zh: 另一方面，供应链攻击也很猖獗。我会至少给自动更新设一个小延迟。除非也许作者本人发帖说明了，但那当然也可能被攻破。

comments.text:
You have to find the balance of when to update vs beware of the supply chain attacks where it's advised to wait out some releases, in some cases hours, in some days.

I think best advice is to skim changelog, watch announcements and security advisories. But no auto-update.
comments.text_zh:
你得找到更新时机和防范供应链攻击之间的平衡，后者往往建议先观望一些版本，有时几小时，有时几天。

我觉得最好的建议是浏览更新日志，关注公告和安全通告。但不要自动更新。

comments.text: Worth adding: auto-upgrades only cover nginx on the host. If you run it in Docker, you’re stuck on whatever the image tag pins.
comments.text_zh: 值得补充：自动升级只覆盖主机上的 nginx。如果你在 Docker 里跑，就只能停在镜像标签锁定的那个版本。

comments.text: that’s a good handy trick!
comments.text_zh: 这是个很实用的小技巧！

comments.text: so this guy think closed all ports and access via some private tunnel is safe when the point is website still exposed on internet.
comments.text_zh: 所以这人觉得关掉所有端口、走某个私有隧道就安全了，可关键是网站仍然暴露在互联网上。

comments.text: https://t.co/dY4MJokCEi
set the auto reboot window to 4am your time and the risky part mostly goes away
comments.text_zh: 把自动重启窗口设到你当地凌晨 4 点，风险大部分就没了

comments.text:
Thats why the less dependencies the better

A library like pingora in a rust server with hard rules may be the safest way to build a secure load balancer
comments.text_zh:
所以依赖越少越好

在 Rust 服务器里用像 pingora 这样带有硬性规则的库，可能是做安全负载均衡最稳妥的办法

comments.text: the scary part isnt nginx its how many ppl are vibe deploying vps boxes rn with zero unattended-upgrades. agents spin up servers way faster than anyone patches them
comments.text_zh: 可怕的不是 nginx，而是现在有多少人正在用 vibe 方式部署 VPS，却完全没开 unattended-upgrades。智能体拉起服务器的速度，远快于任何人去打补丁

comments.text: auto reboot on a box nobody's watching feels like the real gamble. do you stagger reboots across your servers or just let them all go at once?
comments.text_zh: 在没人盯着的机器上自动重启，感觉才是真正的赌博。你会把各台服务器的重启错开，还是让它们一起重启？

translation.summary: NGINX 漏洞很吓人，不过我查过了，我的 VPS 已经自动升级到新版本了！ 现在开启自动升级非常非常非常非常非常重要，我甚至开了自动重启，人不在的时候这样做有点风险，但比起宕机几小时，我更在意网站是最新且安全的 而且一般来说，安全更新/升级都经过测试，是安全的
translation.body:
NGINX 漏洞很吓人，不过我查过了，我的 VPS 已经自动升级到新版本了！

现在开启自动升级非常非常非常非常非常重要，我甚至开了自动重启，人不在的时候这样做有点风险，但比起宕机几小时，我更在意网站是最新且安全的

而且一般来说，安全更新/升级都经过测试，是安全的
translation.label: 机器翻译

items.summary: 💯 There is no real way to survive for most SaaS companies here because AI is so completely different than any technological advancement before it Before you could just niche down and specialize on one…
items.body:
💯

There is no real way to survive for most SaaS companies here because AI is so completely different than any technological advancement before it

Before you could just niche down and specialize on one thing and you'd know for certain the big tech companies would never be able to dedicate enough resources to fill your tiny little niche market of $300M where you could take 1% of the market and make $3M/year

Riches in the niches!

And so you'd avoid going too general, because "you'd spread yourself too thin" and hit "death by a thousand paper cuts"

And general was where big tech companies were great at, they could dedicate huge resources in solving these big problems, like building Google Sheets, or Salesforce (whatever it is they do)

But that was the old days, and it's completely different now

With AI, big tech companies can easily fill any niche, or be general at the same time, they can do the whole range actually, without even spending time on consciously doing that, because they're not offering a particular SaaS offering at all

They're offering you artificial general intelligence (AGI) that can do it all

And as long as they improve their models every time and make them bigger and better, it slowly can do literally anything (okay not yet anything, for anything they'll need physical robots, but they're working on that too of course)

This leaves SaaS companies with a bitter ending:
- they either do nothing and stay in their niche like they economically should, but that doesn't work anymore now
- they try go general, and offer EVERYTHING and ANYTHING, and that works for a little bit until customers realize they might as well use whoever makes the models that the SaaS itself uses anyway, which is the big tech and big AI companies, who by the way either offer it free or for much cheaper

Everyone's been checkmated by big tech and big AI

This will be the creative destruction of the century

But there'll be some survivors and then a lot of new companies, but how they'll look nobody knows yet!
